transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mrs. Fitzgerald. Thank you for meeting with me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Hello doctor. I am still... I feel very sick today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I wanted to talk to you about why you felt so sick during your treatment yesterday. There was a mistake. We forgot to give you the medicine that stops nausea.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Before the chemo, we usually give a medicine to stop you from vomiting. That medicine was not in the order. It was not given to you. That is why you were so sick. Does that make sense to you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. Why?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The medicine that stops the sick feeling was missing. No medicine for the stomach. So you felt very bad. Do you understand now?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I thought... I thought it was just the chemo. It was so scary.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a mistake in the paperwork. We did not check the list correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My husband... he used to hold my hand when I was sick. Now I am alone and I feel this. It is too much.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you are feeling very lonely right now, especially remembering how your husband supported you through the hard times.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: He was my everything. I cannot do this without him. And then the hospital makes a mistake. I feel so small.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see how frightening and overwhelming this is for you, especially when you are missing him so much.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Why did this happen to me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system failed to flag the missing medication and the team did not catch it before the infusion started.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Are you sorry?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am concerned that you had such a difficult experience yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I asked the nurse if I should have the stomach medicine. She said yes, but then nothing happened. I waited and waited. And then I was sick everywhere. It was a nightmare.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you felt ignored and then you suffered through that nightmare.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just so tired. My heart is tired.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is very hard to deal with all of this at once.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this happen again? I cannot do that again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are looking into how to fix the list for next time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is next time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check the schedule and tell you soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to go home.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Let me tell you what we will do now. I will write a new note for the nurses to make sure the nausea medicine is there for every single visit from now on.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How do I know it is there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Next time, you can ask the nurse to show you the medicine bag before it starts. You can ask them, is the nausea medicine here?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not want to be a bother.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are not a bother. It is your health. I will make sure the nursing lead knows to double check.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to feel okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I will go and speak with the nursing team now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go check the chart, but I will be back in a few minutes to see if you are ready to go home.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a regulated pace during emotional distress, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The error (missing nausea medicine) is named in the first turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('Does that make sense to you?' and 'Do you understand now?').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the paperwork' and 'the system'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('lonely', 'frightening', 'overwhelming', 'ignored') and references the patient's specific content regarding her husband.

T.justification: Resident provides a specific next step (new note for nurses), a timeline (next visit), a named patient role (asking to see the bag), and addresses prevention.
